title: Surveillance on California dairy farms reveals multiple possible sources of H5N1 influenza virus transmission
experiments_summary:
The study conducted surveillance on 14 H5N1-positive dairy farms in California from October 2024 to April 2025. Three main areas of investigation were pursued: air sampling, wastewater sampling, and individual cow quarter sampling.

Air sampling: Three devices were compared in an initial phase on five Central Valley farms: (1) open-face PTFE filter cassettes connected to a GilAir 5 personal air sampler pump worn in a backpack; (2) Sartorius MD8 Airport handheld sampler with a cone attachment at 50 L/min; and (3) AirPrep Cub 210 at 200 L/min. Samples were collected from exhaled breath of individual cows and rows of cows in housing pens, within milking parlors during milking, and near wastewater sites. A total of 71 air samples were collected in the initial phase. Based on initial results, subsequent sampling on nine additional farms focused primarily on the MD8 Airport sampler. Particle size quantification in milking parlors was performed using an AeroTrak Handheld Airborne Particle Counter (TSI) measuring six size bins from 0.3–25 µm, and qualitative droplet analysis of MD8 gelatin filters using ImageJ with a custom Python script. Samples were processed by eluting filters into viral transport media (VTM) or brain heart infusion (BHI) media, followed by RNA extraction and RT-qPCR using H5 HA-specific primers and probe on CFX Connect or QuantStudio 5 systems. Air samples positive by RT-qPCR were subjected to viral titration on MDCK cells by plaque assay or TCID50.

Wastewater sampling: Water samples were collected at multiple points along the reclaimed water stream on farms, including milking parlor drains, sump pumps adjacent to the dairy parlor, manure lagoons, and fields where reclaimed water is used. Samples were collected aseptically using 50 mL tubes, 250 mL or 1 L bottles, and a 25-foot extendable pole for inaccessible locations. Raw samples were centrifuged at 16,500g to remove solids, then concentrated using NanoTrap Microbiome Particles on a KingFisher Apex. An endogenous control (bovine respiratory syncytial virus, BRSV) was added before concentration. Nucleic acids were extracted using MagMax Viral Pathogen kit and analyzed by duplex droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) targeting influenza A M gene and H5 HA. Three ddPCR replicates were merged per sample. Selected samples with genome copy concentrations above 650 copies/mL were subjected to viral titration by TCID50 and plaque assay on MDCK cells.

Milking equipment surface sampling: Interior surfaces of milking liners and exterior shells were sampled with pre-moistened flocked swabs in VTM. Swab eluates were processed by vortexing and brief centrifugation, then RNA-extracted and analyzed by RT-qPCR. Positive samples were titrated for infectious virus.

Whole genome sequencing: Nine air samples and one wastewater sample from farm EC were sequenced. RNA was amplified by one-step multiplex RT-PCR using three different primer sets (Uni12/Inf1, Uni12/Inf3, Uni13/Inf1; MBTuni-12, MBTuni-12.4, MBTuni-13; OptiF1, OptiF2, OptiR). Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing was performed on a GridION instrument after barcoding and adapter ligation. Reads were aligned using IRMA, clades assigned via Nextclade, and consensus sequences aligned with MUSCLE in MegAlign Pro. Variants were reported only when present in all consensus sequences from a sample with at least 24-fold coverage depth at a given locus.

Longitudinal individual quarter sampling: Twenty-three cows on farm EC were screened for H5N1 on March 18–19, 2025; 14 were selected for longitudinal sampling. Milk from each of the four quarters (left front, right front, left rear, right rear) was collected daily for seven days by farm workers prior to milking into separate 50 mL conical tubes, stored at 4°C, and shipped to Emory for RT-qPCR and virus titering. Exhaled breath from all study cows was collected on three days using the MD8 Airport sampler.

Antibody detection in milk: Milk was collected from 4 recovered cows and 10 cows without clinical signs on farm FB in April 2025. H5-specific IgG antibodies were measured by ELISA on Immulon 4HBX plates coated with recombinant HA protein from A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002-v/2024(H5N1). Serially diluted milk samples were incubated, detected with peroxidase-conjugated mouse anti-bovine IgG (clone IL-A2), and developed with TMB substrate. A human IgG monoclonal antibody (Fi6v3) dilution series was included on each plate to standardize inter-assay variability.

Biometric monitoring: Biometric data (ankle monitors, Afimilk) from 40 cows on farm FB were used to group animals by clinical outcome during the November 2024 outbreak: culled, recovered, or no signs. Daily milk weight data were used to bracket cows into clinical groups.
